profiles.summary: No new tagged bor release since cycle 26: of 12 candidate tags only v2.12.0-beta exists beyond v2.11.2, and develop core/vm is byte equal to the cycle 26 copy. The 30,108 cycle 27 vectors match on all five private bor builds behind publicnode, on QuikNode and on drpc. Polygon's second client, 0xPolygon/erigon, has no release after v3.7.2, whose chain spec stops at Valencia, so bor is the only client that can follow mainnet.

deltas.delta: Polygon mainnet runs CLZ (EIP-7939) since Lisovo at block 83,756,500 (lisovoInstructionSet at core/vm/jump_table.go:93-97 on develop). An eth_call on bor ebcfea01452d returned 251 for CLZ(0x1e). The PoolManager runtime holds no 0x1e byte at an instruction position in a linear sweep of its 24,009 bytes, so the opcode never runs.

0xPolygon/erigon v3.7.2 is the last tag (v3.7.3, v3.8.0, v3.8.1 and v3.9.0 return 404) and its bor-mainnet chain spec ends at valenciaBlock 89,531,000. Austin (91,949,700), Uburu (96,787,900) and Salvador (98,688,600) are absent, so no Erigon node can import current blocks. Tatum records that Polygon ended Erigon support on 1 August 2026.

findings.title: Polygon has one execution client that can follow mainnet, because the 0xPolygon/erigon line stopped before the Austin fork
findings.difference: Ethereum has several execution clients, so an arithmetic fault in one is outvoted. On Polygon the last 0xPolygon/erigon tag is v3.7.2, whose mainnet chain spec ends at Valencia (block 89,531,000). Austin, Uburu and Salvador are missing, so every Polygon validator and full node runs bor.
findings.mechanism: Every swap computes FullMath.mulDiv, which calls MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24) and, when the product needs more than 256 bits, with the pool's denominator (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:48). On Polygon, opMulmod is the only implementation of that result. The current bor v2.11.1 builds use stock holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 MulMod. The unreleased v2.12.0-beta and develop route full-width moduli through a one-entry reciprocal memo (core/vm/mulmod_memo.go:55-66), and its result equals MulMod for every input because MulModWithReciprocal and MulMod run the same reduce4 call on the same reciprocal (uint256.go:688-748). No second client would catch a future fault in that path. Today every vector, script and mined swap matches.
findings.impact: None today. If a future bor release computed a wrong MULMOD or shift result, the chain would accept it, and swaps would pay amounts that differ from the source. Who gains depends on the fault.
findings.preconditions: A fault would have to ship in a bor release that block producers run. No ordinary account can cause one.
findings.mitigations: Before each bor release that touches core/vm (the MULMOD memo of v2.12.0 first), rerun battery.py, targeted.py, run_edges.py and the memo sequences of cycles/026/established-l1.work/memoseq.py against a node on that release.

cleared.check: bor's MULMOD memo against holiman/uint256 v1.3.2, the version develop pins (go.mod line 59), and whether a newer uint256 exists.
cleared.result: opMulmod pops x and y by value and passes the stack top as z (core/vm/instructions.go:200-205). The memo copies the modulus before computing Reciprocal(z) and reuses it only when all four limbs equal (mulmod_memo.go:55-63). MulModWithReciprocal (uint256.go:688-715) and MulMod (720-748) run identical code except that MulMod computes Reciprocal(m) on line 728, so the result is a pure function of x, y and m. The Go module proxy lists v1.3.2 as the newest uint256 release.

cleared.check: CLZ (EIP-7939) is live on Polygon (Lisovo) and BNB Chain, refused on Avalanche. Does the PoolManager bytecode ever execute 0x1e?
cleared.result: A linear sweep of the 24,009 byte runtime read from the Polygon PoolManager finds no 0x1e at an instruction position; the first INVALID is at offset 23,996, where the metadata area starts. The source uses no clz (BitMath.sol:12 and :31 use table lookups), so the opcode set difference changes nothing for the pool math.

cleared.check: L-1148 for BNB Chain: any per-EVM arithmetic cache like bor's memo in BSC v1.8.2, master or develop.
cleared.result: None. opMulmod is z.MulMod(&x, &y, z) at core/vm/instructions.go:179-183 on all three refs, and master equals v1.8.2 byte for byte. The EVM struct (core/vm/evm.go:129-171) holds context, StateDB, jump table, depth, config, precompiles, a jump destination cache keyed by code hash and a pooled stack arena, and no operand or result cache. BSC pins holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 on v1.8.2 and develop.

cleared.check: L-1148 for Avalanche: any per-EVM arithmetic cache in libevm, at the commit avalanchego 1.15.3 pins (d398bc4dbe41) and at main.
cleared.result: None. opMulmod is stock at core/vm/instructions.go:183-187, the EVM struct adds only executionInvalidated (evm.go:133), and instructions.go equals go-ethereum v1.13.15 apart from import paths. The cycle 26 reading was made at a335c2ecf4df, which master pins; the seven core/vm files compared are byte equal between the two commits.

cleared.check: L-1073: how reth-bsc keys storage and transient storage and whether it carries the Hertz shared storage path.
cleared.result: reth-bsc 23b510f uses revm 38.0.0 with revm-interpreter 35.0.1 and ruint 1.18.0 (Cargo.lock) and the stock EthInstructions table (src/evm/api/mod.rs:74-90). Storage and transient storage are revm's maps keyed by address and full U256 slot. The Hertz fix is a table of fixed historical mainnet transaction hashes whose slots are written before or after those transactions on import only (src/node/evm/patch/mod.rs:16-708, executor.rs:818-822, 931); it has no shared storage read path, and no patched address is the PoolManager.

cleared.check: reth-bsc's own frame rule for the block coinbase.
cleared.result: A frame whose target is the coinbase halts with PrecompileError and burns its gas (src/evm/api/mod.rs:237-268). That frame is a call to the validator's own address, which only the party naming the address can arrange, as recipient of its own take or as a hook address it chose. A coinbase account without code is paid normally because revm returns before frame_run for empty code.

cleared.check: Which validators could run a code path other than the public endpoint's on Polygon: is Erigon still a validator client?
cleared.result: No. The last 0xPolygon/erigon tag is v3.7.2 and its chain spec ends at Valencia, and Austin, Uburu and Salvador are missing, so an Erigon node cannot import current blocks. All validators run bor. The differences left are the private v2.11.1 builds and the BlockSTM parallel processor, which cycle 26 read as byte identical between v2.11.1, v2.11.2 and v2.12.0-beta.

cleared.check: L-1131: the selector 0xcea9e31d of the failed transaction 0x52cea783...c269.
cleared.result: It is InsufficientReturnAmount() of ParaSwap's AugustusV6 at 0x6a000f20005980200259b80c5102003040001068 (verified source from routescan, src/interfaces/IErrors.sol:12). The transaction calls swapExactAmountIn (selector 0xe3ead59e), which runs its executor and then reverts at src/routers/swapExactAmountIn/GenericSwapExactAmountIn.sol:85-86 when the received balance is below minAmountOut. The revert is the router's slippage check after the executor, and with it the PoolManager unlock, returned. The same call succeeds at the parent block and fails at its own block because earlier transactions moved the price.

leadResults.answer: All 30,108 vectors (15,510 large-index and 14,598 edge) return the specified word on Polygon (each of the five private bor builds behind publicnode, QuikNode v2.11.1 hosts and drpc), BNB Chain (dataseed1 v1.8.2-4e1c8247 and v1.8.2 without commit, 48 Club 132104cd and 9b93ce23, reth-bsc 23b510f) and Avalanche (avalanchego 1.15.3 on two endpoints). Per-build counts are in cycles/028/established-l1.work/out/edges-*.json.

For this unit's clients: BSC v1.8.2, master and develop and libevm d398bc4dbe41 (pinned by avalanchego 1.15.3), a335c2ecf4df and main all call stock MulMod, and their EVM structs hold no operand or result cache. BSC has a pooled stack arena and a jump destination cache keyed by code hash, both from go-ethereum. Nitro's submodule at b72783f and geth's next release belong to other units and were not read here.

Script set 1 and set 2 were rerun through polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com, whose five private builds all gave the stored hashes on the edge vectors with matching brackets. pmdiff.py does not record the build per call, so the set 1 result (231 of 250, the recorded 19 gas-limited scripts different) is not pinned to one build. 25 multi-step swaps replay to the unit from state read on QuikNode bor v2.11.1. The theme-state-replay window was not rerun.
Not continued this cycle; carried as a new low lead with the same collector. The PoolManager window on BNB Chain is still 14,274 traced transactions with no mismatch.

reth-bsc 23b510f keys storage and transient storage by address and full U256 slot through stock revm 38.0.0 and revm-interpreter 35.0.1. Its Hertz equivalent is a set of storage writes tied to fixed historical transaction hashes, applied only on import (src/node/evm/patch/mod.rs:16-708, src/node/evm/executor.rs:818-822 and 931), with no shared storage read path.

0xcea9e31d is InsufficientReturnAmount() of AugustusV6 at 0x6a00...1068. The transaction calls swapExactAmountIn, and GenericSwapExactAmountIn.sol:85-86 reverts with it after the executor returned, when the received balance is below minAmountOut. The PoolManager did not make the decision.

The failed transaction is explained by L-1131 as a router slippage revert after the PoolManager returned. The 5,259 untraced window transactions remain, because no public Avalanche endpoint serves debug_traceTransaction (cycle 26 probe, unchanged).

Avalanche has no scheduled fork in the next six months: Igloo is UnscheduledActivationTime on mainnet and Fuji (avalanchego master upgrade/upgrade.go:69 and 94), and no published ACP was found that adds EIP-2537 at 0x0b to 0x11. P-256 at 0x100 is already live since Granite. A payout to those addresses affects only the caller's own take. HyperEVM belongs to another unit.
